doc: Material classes of the tier-1 physics layer (docs/design/TIER1_PHYSICS.md 4.3; read through house_sim/kernel/phys/props.py). Every material string a type declares maps to one class through `aliases`; a type chain that declares no material falls back to its supports.json row `material`, then to `category_material` (keys: type, is_a or category), then to plastic. Numbers are lumped household values (fidelity P-approx); `source` cites the reasoning and `anchor` the behaviour a test pins (tests/test_physics_data.py).

columns.rho: bulk density of the solid, kg/m3
columns.break_mode: how a break shows: shatter (brittle), chip (enamel, stone and engineered-wood edges), crack (screens, rigid plastic, wax), bruise (food); null: does not break from a household drop
columns.drop_tol_m: survivable drop height onto a floor of impact hardness 1.0 (tile); null: unbreakable (inf)
columns.crush_kg: load resting on top before it is crushed or broken; null: unlimited (inf)
columns.mu: dry static friction against finished wood (manipulation's FRICTION table)
columns.abs: absorption capacity, litres of water per kg of dry mass
columns.hard: impact hardness of this material as a landing or support surface (tile 1.0)
columns.heat: heat limit of this material as a support finish, deg C (a hotter item marks it); null: no limit
columns.melt: melting or softening point, deg C; null: does not melt in a house
columns.shock: thermal-shock tolerance, kelvin of sudden temperature difference; null: not shock-sensitive
columns.mohs: finish hardness on the Mohs scale (scratching)
columns.wsens: water sensitivity 0 (unaffected) to 1 (ruined by standing water)
columns.compressible: textile volume that squeezes when packed (containment counts volume x (1 - 0.5 x softness))
columns.mu_wet: friction when wet, replacing the generic wet factor (soap)
columns.wet_strength: strength factor when soaked (corrugated board loses most of its compression strength)
columns.floats: a solid piece of this material floats in fresh water once its pores have flooded (density below 1000 kg/m3: wood, cork, wax, polyethylene and polypropylene, foams); absent: it sinks. Sealed hollow things (closed containers, balls, inflatables) float by their own mass and outline instead (props.Phys.floats)

glass.source: annealed soda-lime glass (tumblers, jars, vases): 2.5 g/cm3, c_p 0.84 J/gK; annealed glass tolerates a sudden 40-50 K difference
glass.anchor: a tumbler dropped from counter height (0.9 m) onto tile breaks; from 0.3 m it survives

tempered_glass.source: toughened soda-lime glass (EN 12150: table tops, oven and shower doors, glass shelves): 4-5x the bending strength of annealed glass, about 150 K thermal shock

borosilicate.source: borosilicate 3.3 (Pyrex lab glass and bakeware): 2.23 g/cm3, expansion 3.3e-6/K, tolerates about 160 K of thermal shock

glass_ceramic.source: glass-ceramic cooktop panels (Ceran class): near-zero thermal expansion, service temperature about 700 C

crystal.source: lead crystal stemware: about 3.1 g/cm3, thin stems and rims
crystal.anchor: stemware breaks from about 0.25 m onto tile

porcelain.source: vitrified porcelain (fine dinnerware, sinks, toilets): hard glaze about Mohs 7, thermal shock about 120 K

stoneware.source: stoneware mugs, crocks and slow-cooker inserts: denser and tougher than earthenware, about 100 K thermal shock

ceramic.source: everyday glazed dinnerware, mugs and tiles sold as ceramic (vitrified stoneware-like bodies): about 2.0 g/cm3; about 100 K downshock, as stoneware (porcelain 120, low-fired terracotta 80): cold water into a just-emptied 90 C mug or a dishwasher-hot plate into cold water does not crack it, a fridge-cold casserole into a 220 C oven (coupling 0.5: 108 K) usually does
ceramic.anchor: plates and mugs break from table height (0.75 m) onto tile and survive carpet (0.75 x 0.35 = 0.26 m < 0.45 m)

terracotta.source: unglazed terracotta pots: porous, about 12 % water uptake by mass

eggshell.source: calcite eggshell: a hen's egg cracks from a few centimetres onto a hard floor; static crushing strength about 3-4 kg end-on, about 1 kg for a sideways load

enameled_metal.source: porcelain enamel on steel (bathtubs, ranges, enamelware): the steel body survives, the glassy enamel chips

stone.source: granite, marble, slate: 2.65-2.75 g/cm3; dropped pieces chip at edges; granite and tile tolerate hot pans above 300 C

concrete.source: concrete, brick and shingle: 2.3 g/cm3, porous (a few % water uptake)

plaster.source: gypsum plaster and drywall: about 0.7-1.0 g/cm3, soft (Mohs 2), crumbles and sags when wet

granular.source: loose soil, sand, salt, litter: bulk density 1.2-1.6 t/m3; a pile has no strength to lose

steel.source: carbon and stainless steel: 7.85 g/cm3, c_p 0.49 J/gK; wsens 0.1 for rust on plain steel

cast_iron.source: grey cast iron cookware and grates: 7.2 g/cm3, c_p 0.46 J/gK; can crack under a large sudden quench; rusts when left wet

aluminum.source: aluminium alloys: 2.7 g/cm3, c_p 0.90 J/gK, melts at 660 C; thin pans and cans dent rather than break

soft_metal.source: brass, copper, silver, gold: 8.5-8.9 g/cm3 for brass and copper, c_p 0.385 J/gK (copper), melting 900-1085 C

film.source: polyethylene film, foil laminates, mylar: LDPE 0.92 g/cm3, c_p 1.9 J/gK, softens and melts about 105-115 C

plastic.source: rigid household plastics (PP, PS, ABS, HDPE, PVC, melamine): 0.9-1.4 g/cm3, c_p 1.3-1.9 J/gK; mouldings survive ordinary drops. As a support finish the heat limit is the softening point under the light pressure of a cup or dish, not the load-bearing heat deflection (0.45 MPa: HDPE about 80 C, PS 90-95, ABS 95-100, PP 100-120, melamine 120-150; Vicat softening 85-150 C): 100 C nominal (the spec table's 80 C is the lowest deflection figure), so trays and garden tables take a mug of boiling water (contact about 80 C) and a hot pan still melts them
plastic.anchor: a mug of boiling water never marks a plastic tray (contact 80 C < 100 x 0.85)

foam_plastic.source: expanded polystyrene (EPS packaging blocks, peanuts): 15-30 kg/m3, softens near 100 C

foam.source: open-cell polyurethane and cellulose sponge foam: 25-60 kg/m3; a sponge holds 10-20x its dry mass of water
foam.anchor: a sponge holds 10-20x its dry mass

closed_cell_foam.source: closed-cell foams (EVA play mats and foam rollers, polyethylene and PVC buoyancy foam in life jackets and ring buoys, XLPE): 30-200 kg/m3; the sealed cells take up almost no water (under about 1 % by volume after immersion; 0.05 L per kg covers the surface film), so they stay light and float; EVA and polyethylene foams soften from about 70 C and melt near 100 C
closed_cell_foam.anchor: a life jacket or a ring buoy floats and soaks up next to nothing

rubber.source: natural, nitrile and silicone rubber: 1.1-1.3 g/cm3, high grip (about 0.9 on wood); silicone is rated to about 230 C

paper.source: paper and card: 0.7-1.2 g/cm3, c_p 1.34 J/gK, absorbs about twice its mass, chars and ignites above 230 C

lined_paperboard.source: polyethylene-coated liquid cartons (Tetra Pak class): liquid-tight, the board still softens at cut edges

cardboard.source: single-wall corrugated board: board density 100-150 kg/m3; a medium box stacks about 15 kg; box compression strength roughly halves at high moisture (x0.4 used for a soaked box)

cotton.source: cotton, linen and canvas textiles: folded bulk 0.2-0.4 g/cm3; a terry towel holds 2.5-3x its dry mass; scorches above about 200 C
cotton.anchor: a terry towel holds 2.5-3x its dry mass

synthetic_fabric.source: polyester, nylon, fleece: hydrophobic fibres hold about 0.6x their mass between them; nylon melts 220 C, polyester 250-260 C

coated_fabric.source: PVC or PU coated polyester (covers, oilcloth): waterproof face; PVC coating softens about 160-200 C

wool.source: wool and felt: very absorbent (about 3x its mass when soaked), scorches rather than melts

leather.source: tanned leather and suede: 0.8-1.0 g/cm3; water stains and stiffens it, heat above about 80 C shrinks it

wood.source: solid wood with a lacquer or oil finish: 0.5-0.75 g/cm3, c_p 1.7 J/gK; the finish shows white heat or moisture rings from about 60 C; mu 0.55 is manipulation's FRICTION value (the spec table's 0.5 was a typo)
wood.anchor: a hot item above 60 C marks a finished wood table

engineered_wood.source: MDF, particleboard, plywood (flat-pack furniture): 0.6-0.8 g/cm3; edges and corners chip when dropped; swells permanently when soaked

laminate.source: high-pressure decorative laminate (worktops, laminate tubes): 1.35 g/cm3, resists about 120 C briefly; swells at seams

wicker.source: rattan and willow wicker baskets: light, springy weave

electronics.source: consumer electronics (plastic or glass-fronted cases with boards and batteries): screens crack; phone makers rate drops of about 1 m (MIL-STD-810G 516.6 uses 1.2 m); liquid ingress ruins them. Nominal 1.2 m so that the whole +-15 % variation band (1.02-1.38 m) survives the 1 m anchor
electronics.anchor: a phone survives a 1 m drop onto tile (every instance: 1.2 x 0.85 > 1.0)

wax.source: paraffin candle wax: 0.9 g/cm3, c_p 2.1-2.9 J/gK, melts 46-68 C (container candles about 50 C)

soap.source: bar soap: firm and grippy dry, about 0.1 friction when wet; dissolves in standing water

organic.source: food and plant tissue: mostly water (c_p 3-4 kJ/kgK, about 1 g/cm3); produce bruises from about 1 m

intangible.source: liquid bodies, flames, residues and marks: no solid body (liquid behaviour comes from liquids.json)

quartz.source: engineered quartz worktops (about 93 % quartz in polyester resin): makers warn of resin scorch above about 150 C

pewter.source: pewter (about 92 % tin with antimony and copper): 7.3 g/cm3, c_p about 0.22 J/gK, melts 170-230 C, soft (Mohs about 1.5); not for the oven (cleaning's adoption request 12)

titanium.source: titanium: 4.5 g/cm3, c_p 0.52 J/gK, melts at 1668 C, hard and corrosion-proof (cleaning's adoption request 12)

hdpe.source: HDPE: 0.94-0.97 g/cm3, lighter than water (milk jugs and bins float); otherwise a rigid household plastic

polypropylene.source: polypropylene: 0.90-0.91 g/cm3, lighter than water; otherwise a rigid household plastic

fiberglass.source: woven E-glass cloth (the only household user is the fire blanket): rated for about 550 C contact, softens near 840 C, non-combustible; the spec's plastic alias would make a fire blanket melt at 120 C

nylon_foam.source: a nylon shell over closed-cell buoyancy foam (life jackets: PVC or polyethylene foam; USCG-approved devices must not take up water)

pva.source: PVA chamois and PVA sponges hold about 12x their dry mass

cellulose.source: every type declaring cellulose is a cellulose sponge, which holds 10-20x its dry mass (the spec listed cellulose under paper, which holds 2x)

polypropylene_fleece.source: polypropylene fibre (0.91 g/cm3) floats even soaked, unlike polyester (1.38) and nylon (1.14)

microfiber.source: split polyester-polyamide microfibre cloth holds about 4x its dry mass

crayon.source: crayon wax (paraffin with pigment) softens and melts about 55-65 C

painted_satin.source: a paint film: the class comes from what is painted (category fallback)

painted_flat.source: a paint film: the class comes from what is painted (category fallback)

upholstered.source: furniture whose material is a fabric or leather is upholstered: a wood or metal frame under padding and a cover. Only the cushions and cover soak up liquid, about 0.3 L per kg of the whole piece (the sofa and armchair rows' value: a 6 kg fabric dining chair holds about 2 L, not the 15 L of 6 kg of cotton)

absorb_volume_cap.source: water can fill only a body's pores, which are less than its outline: a body holds at most 90 % of its volume (box x 0.785 for cylinders, 0.524 for spheres). A 10 L sandbag cannot take 25 L; open-cell sponges (porosity 95-98 %) stay under it

fragile_default.source: a record marked fragile whose class never breaks gets the strength of annealed glass (0.5 m, 10 kg): the author says it can break

crushable.source: manipulation's max_load rule (TIER1_PHYSICS 5.3 keeps it): only items that declare a crush or load limit, are fragile or crushable, or get a crush_kg from a supports.json row can be crushed; besides them, boxes and cartons (corrugated board, lined paperboard) and eggs crumple by nature. A stack of books, notebooks or plastic bins is never crushed by its own weight. A crushable record whose class has no crush limit gives way under 5 kg (manipulation DEFAULT_FRAGILE)

heat_resistant_c.source: trivets, hot pads, oven racks, stovetops and sink basins take a pan straight from the oven (about 250 C) with margin; `heat_resistant: true` raises the heat limit to at least this

surface_state_mu.source: manipulation SURFACE_STATE_MU, unchanged (a film of water roughly halves dry friction; soap or oil films cut it to about a tenth)

pair_reference.source: class mu values are measured against finished wood, so a pair a-b is mu_a x mu_b / mu_wood (a material on wood gets exactly its own column)
